title: Multiply and divide integers
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

sections.title: Multiply integers
sections.objective: Multiply the sizes, then use the sign rule.
explain: 3 × (−4) means 3 groups of −4: −4 + (−4) + (−4) = −12. A positive times a negative is negative.
Look at the pattern: 3 × (−4) = −12, 2 × (−4) = −8, 1 × (−4) = −4, 0 × (−4) = 0. Each step goes up by 4, so the next ones are −1 × (−4) = 4 and −2 × (−4) = 8. A negative times a negative is positive.

The rule: multiply the sizes, then count the negative numbers. An even number of negatives gives a positive answer; an odd number gives a negative answer. −2 × 3 × (−5) has two negatives, so it's +30.

sections.title: Divide integers
sections.objective: Divide the sizes, then use the same sign rule.
explain: Dividing follows the same sign rule as multiplying, because every division is a multiplication backwards: −42 ÷ 6 = −7 because 6 × (−7) = −42.
Divide the sizes (42 ÷ 6 = 7), then the sign: one negative gives a negative answer, two negatives give a positive answer. −42 ÷ (−7) = 6.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.objective: Multiply and divide integers, mixed together.
explain: Multiply or divide the sizes. Then count the negative numbers: even gives positive, odd gives negative.
